There is no sponsor, guarantor or borrower distinct from the registrant in the context.

facts.text: - Financial reports: statements of earnings, comprehensive income, financial position, equity and cash flows, and notes, are all present in the latest quarterly report and the annual report (index at latest quarterly report page:2 and annual report page:202). Borrowings note, latest quarterly report page:57 "Total borrowings $ 17,025 $ 15,182"; balance sheet, page:39 "Total borrowings 17,025 15,182"; unsecured note ladder, page:28 "Total senior and subordinated unsecured notes $ 8,150"; securitized maturities, page:26 "Total borrowings—owed to securitization investors $ 3,900 $ 5,025 $ — $ — $ 8,925". Facility-level debt is therefore located. Carrying value and principal are shown on different bases (unamortised discounts, premiums and issuance costs), which CP-1 must keep apart. - Liquidity and funding: latest quarterly report page:29 "$19.5 billion of liquid assets" and "we had an aggregate of $13.0 billion of available borrowing capacity through the Federal Reserve’s discount window"; annual report page:91 "we had an aggregate of $2.1 billion of undrawn credit facilities". Cash flows: page:41 "Total cash and equivalents, including restricted amounts, at end of period $ 16,697 $ 16,287". - Capital: latest quarterly report page:60 "Synchrony Financial met all minimum capital requirements" and the capital table quoted above. - Covenants: latest quarterly report page:28 "We were in compliance with all of these covenants at September 30, 2026"; annual report page:57 "we were not in default under any of our credit facilities". Only a general statement is supplied. - Securitization triggers: latest quarterly report page:27 "No early amortization event has occurred". Subsequent event within the filing: page:27 "which matured and were repaid in October 2026". - Business and transaction narrative: annual report page:9 "Home & Auto accounted for $5.7 billion, or 26%, of our total interest and fees on loans for the year ended December 31, 2025"; acquisition, latest quarterly report page:47 "In April 2026, we completed our acquisition of the Lowe's commercial co-branded credit card portfolio". facts.label: Evidence to risk to consequence
facts.text: - Evidence: the latest quarterly report gives funding by instrument family (securitized, unsecured, deposits) and a covenant compliance statement, but the indentures are only incorporated by reference. Source risk: the unsecured notes' covenant package, events of default and any cross-default or acceleration terms cannot be read, only the issuer's compliance statement. Consequence: covenant headroom and legal ranking are recorded as Not supplied, and CP-1 must not present covenant tests as measured. - Evidence: year-end capital ratios differ between the annual report and the latest quarterly report because of a disclosed presentation change. Source risk: a trend line that joins the two bases would show a spurious capital change. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must state the basis of each ratio and use the recast basis for sequential comparison. - Evidence: the releases name a financial supplement and a non-GAAP reconciliation that are absent. Source risk: tangible common equity, return on tangible common equity and the recast comparatives rest on management statements. Consequence: these metrics stay attributed management claims, and a filing figure controls whenever the two differ. - Evidence: full-year cash paid for interest and taxes appears only in the annual report. Source risk: interim coverage measures lack a cash-paid input. Consequence: such measures are Not calculable for Q3 2026 and the nine-month period from filed cash-paid data. - Evidence: the entity roles span holding company, bank and consolidated trusts. Source risk: trust assets support trust notes and bank deposits fund the bank, so consolidated totals can hide structural subordination. Consequence: downstream debt work should split parent, bank and securitization claims and not rely on a single consolidated total.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Financial base view: the pinned filings give a complete reported base for the consolidated issuer at four balance-sheet dates (FY2025, Q1 2026, Q2 2026, Q3 2026) and for the nine months of 2026, with year-on-year comparatives. Leverage in the sense the chart tables ask for is Not supplied because the issuer reports no EBITDA and treats interest expense as an operating cost within net interest income. The funding structure is deposit-led, with securitized borrowings and unsecured notes as the borrowed layers; the unsecured layer grew most in 2026 through the February and July issuances. Capital is reported above the stated minimums and the Company and the Bank are stated as well capitalized, but year-end 2025 capital ratios exist on two bases because of a presentation recast, and one earlier handoff statement is corrected below. Interim cash-paid interest and tax are Not supplied, so no cash interest cover can be built for 2026 periods. Nothing in this base is a credit opinion; the CP-2 synthesis owns that.

facts.label: Liquidity, capital and ratings
facts.text: - Liquid assets of 19.5 billion at 2026-09-30 (16.6 billion at 2025-12-31); discount window availability of 13.0 billion; undrawn securitization capacity of 2.6 billion of which 2.1 billion is committed and 450 million uncommitted (10-Q Q3 page:29). Loans pledged by the Bank to the discount window were 18.4 billion (10-Q Q3 page:47). - Capital: the Company and the Bank are stated as meeting well-capitalized requirements (10-Q Q3 page:60). On the recast basis the common equity Tier 1 ratio moved from 13.5 percent at 2025-12-31 to 13.2 percent at Q2 2026 and 12.9 percent at Q3 2026, alongside purchases of treasury stock of 2,878 and common dividends of 314 in the nine months of 2026 (10-Q Q3 pages:60 and 41). The parent relies on Bank dividends; 10-K Note 16 shows parent-only cash and equivalents of 2,465 at 2025-12-31 and dividends from bank subsidiaries of 2,700 in FY2025, with restricted net assets of subsidiaries of 14.7 billion (10-K pages:193 and 194). No parent-only statements are printed for 2026 interim periods. - Ratings as printed by the issuer: Synchrony Financial senior unsecured BBB- (S&P) and BBB (Fitch); outlook Positive at S&P and Stable at Fitch at 2026-09-30, against Stable at both at 2025-12-31 (10-Q Q3 page:28; 10-K page:57). The agency reports are not in the pack. - Covenants: the 10-K describes the indenture covenants as restrictions on disposing of or placing liens on the Bank voting stock and on any merger or sale that leaves the Bank less than 80 percent controlled; compliance and no default are stated (10-K page:57; 10-Q Q3 page:28). No leverage or coverage maintenance test is printed.

facts.label: Corrections to the earlier handoff and definition risks
facts.text: - Correction to the source readiness handoff: that handoff recorded covenant terms as supplied only in general terms; the annual report does state the covenant types (control of the Bank at 80 percent and lien and disposal limits on its voting stock), as quoted above. Test levels and the full indenture text remain unavailable. The earlier handoff is not edited and this answer governs. - Capital recast: year-end 2025 common equity Tier 1 appears as 12.6 percent in the annual report and 13.5 percent in the Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 reports, because internal-use capitalized software was reclassified from intangible assets (10-K page:149 intangible assets 1,255; 10-Q Q3 page:39 intangible assets 104 for the same date). The Q1 2026 ratio is on the earlier basis, so the move from Q1 to Q2 2026 mixes a basis change with performance. - Carrying value and principal differ by unamortised discounts, premiums and issuance costs; the chart tables use principal, the financials table uses carrying value. - Asset acquisition: the annual report expected the Lowe's commercial portfolio at about 0.8 billion; the completed purchase in April 2026 was 0.7 billion (10-K page:34; 10-Q Q3 page:47). The filed completed figure controls. - Net earnings fell against the prior-year third quarter (892 against 1,077); the Q3 2026 release attributes this to a higher provision for credit losses (a reserve build against a reserve release in the prior-year quarter), higher other expense and higher retailer share arrangements, partly offset by higher net interest income (release page:2, attributed management statement). Nine-month net charge-offs fell (3,946 against 4,297, 10-Q Q3 page:14).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Business and transaction view: Synchrony is a consumer financing company that issues private label, dual, co-brand and general purpose credit cards, installment loans and deposit products through partner programs in five sales platforms. Its economics are tied to a short list of partner programs, the sharing of program performance through retailer share arrangements, a deposit-led funding model and heavy regulation as a savings and loan holding company with a bank subsidiary. There is no sponsor-led or leveraged transaction in the sources: the transaction section therefore records one completed asset purchase (a commercial card portfolio), the 2026 senior note, preferred stock and securitized issuance, and a larger share buyback programme. For a creditor the central questions are partner concentration and renewal, whether shareholder distributions are outrunning earnings, and how much of the funding stack sits at the holding company rather than the bank. The facts below separate what the filings state from management language and from analyst reading.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: There is no sponsor-led, merger, leveraged buyout or refinancing transaction in the sources, and the run context lists no deal terms, so the transaction area carries one Insufficient Information entry for any such transaction and does not infer one. What the sources do document in the period is the following. In April 2026 the company completed the acquisition of loan receivables associated with the Lowe's commercial co-branded credit card portfolio, which it accounted for as an asset purchase and reports within Home & Auto; the annual report had expected the purchase at about 0.8 billion in the first half of 2026 and the completed amount reported is 0.7 billion, and the filed completed figure controls. New debt in 2026 was senior unsecured notes issued by Synchrony Financial in February 2026 (750) and in July 2026 (1.1 billion in two fixed-to-floating series, 600 due October 2030 and 500 due July 2037), against 500 of repayments of senior unsecured notes in the nine months; the printed ladder includes all series with their dates and rates. Securitized debt proceeds were 1,495 in the nine months against 1,000 of repayments, and the Q3 report records 750 of fixed securitized borrowings repaid in October 2026 as an event inside the filing. Preferred equity funding was the June 2026 issue of depositary shares representing 500 of Series C preferred stock at a 7.250 percent reset rate, with the first dividend in August 2026. On the distribution side the April 2026 board action approved a new repurchase programme of up to 6.5 billion with no expiry and a planned quarterly dividend increase to 0.34 per share beginning in the third quarter, and about 4.6 billion of authorisation remained at 2026-09-30. Debt raised and its liquidity effect are shown in the CP-1 handoff; use of proceeds is not stated for the notes, so it is Not supplied. The latest filing is dated 2026-10-22 and no transaction after that date is in any source.

facts.text: - Ownership: a listed company with no sponsor and no controlling holder identified in the sources. Percentages, control rights and economic interests are Not supplied; none are inferred. - Legal capacity: the unsecured note covenants described in the filings limit liens on, and loss of control of, the Bank's voting stock; no leverage test or restricted-payments test is printed. Regulatory limits on dividends and repurchases at the parent and on dividends from the Bank apply (10-Q Q3 pages:30, 32). The documents permitting distributions are therefore not supplied in full. - Willingness (documented actions): in the nine months of 2026 the company repurchased 2.9 billion of common stock and paid common dividends of 314 and preferred dividends of 70 (10-Q Q3 pages:12, 41); issued 500 of Series C preferred (net proceeds 494); issued 1,850 of senior unsecured notes against 500 repaid; and raised the quarterly common dividend. facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability: Evidence: the five largest programs were 54 percent of interest and fees, with expiry dates from 2030 to 2035 (F1, 10-K pages:13, 14). Risk mechanic: a single non-renewal or a partner purchase of accounts would remove a large block of receivables and fee income, while long terms give visibility to the contract dates. Credit implication: monitoring posture should track renewals and partner health; revenue visibility is high until 2030 and concentrated afterwards. The counter-evidence is the extension of the Amazon agreement and the new OnePay programme in 2025. - Margin and cash-flow risk: Evidence: retailer share payments rose while net charge-offs fell (F14), and other expense rose with technology and operating losses. Risk mechanic: the sharing of program performance caps the benefit of better credit, so margin gains from lower losses are shared, while cost growth is not shared. Credit implication: debt service capacity is supported by earnings that remain well above interest cost, but margin resilience depends on credit staying at current levels. The earnings fall against the prior-year quarter is a named counter to a stable-margin view. - Concentration risk: Evidence: three partners each over a tenth of interest and fees (F1). Risk mechanic: partner financial distress or a pricing dispute would affect volume, receivables quality and share payments together. Credit implication: concentration should be a monitoring item; no recovery conclusion is drawn here. - Capital allocation and sponsor alignment: Evidence: distributions exceeded net earnings in the nine months alongside new securities issuance (Ownership, governance and capital allocation). Risk mechanic: returning capital faster than it is earned lowers the equity cushion, and new senior notes at the holding company add claims that rank behind the Bank's deposits and the trusts' secured notes in terms of asset access. Credit implication: the key uncertainty is the pace of buybacks against the capital ratio and rating-agency targets; no sponsor exists to provide external support. - Key uncertainties: executed indentures, contract terms, ownership percentages and the financial supplement are Not supplied; a logged conflict of presentation (the capital recast) counters any simple year-over-year capital trend.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Synchrony Financial has a sound fundamental credit profile with moderate, identifiable risks. The strongest support is deposit-led funding (USD 82,951 million of deposits against USD 17,025 million of borrowings at 2026-09-30), liquid assets of USD 19.5 billion and a common equity Tier 1 ratio of 12.9% that the company states exceeds regulatory minimums, with a net charge-off rate of 4.79% in Q3 2026. The weakest point is concentration: five partner programs produced 54% of interest and fees, and distributions of USD 3,262 million in the nine months of 2026 exceeded net earnings of USD 2,582 million. What decides the outcome is whether partners renew and credit losses stay near current levels while buybacks continue to lower the capital ratio.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

citations.quote: Synchrony Financial has a sound fundamental credit profile with moderate, identifiable risks. The strongest support is deposit-led funding (USD 82,951 million of deposits against USD 17,025 million of borrowings at 2026-09-30), liquid assets of USD 19.5 billion and a common equity Tier 1 ratio of 12.9% that the company states exceeds regulatory minimums, with a net charge-off rate of 4.79% in Q3 2026. The weakest point is concentration: five partner programs produced 54% of interest and fees, and distributions of USD 3,262 million in the nine months of 2026 exceeded net earnings of USD 2,582 million. What decides the outcome is whether partners renew and credit losses stay near current levels while buybacks continue to lower the capital ratio.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Synchrony Financial funds its balance sheet mainly with deposits, which were USD 82,951 million at 2026-09-30 and 83% of funding sources, while borrowings were USD 17,025 million. Because debt due within one year of that date was USD 4,500 million against liquid assets of USD 19.5 billion, near-term maturities are covered several times by liquidity even before counting the USD 2,100 million of undrawn committed securitization capacity. This lowers refinancing and liquidity risk for creditors, and the main condition is continued access to deposits and the Federal Reserve discount window, whose availability was USD 13.0 billion.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business depends on a short list of partners. The five largest programs produced 54% of interest and fees and 52% of loan receivables at year-end 2025, and three of them each exceeded a tenth of interest and fees; contract expiry dates run from 2030 to 2035, and some agreements let the partner buy the accounts on termination. A loss or repricing of one program would reduce revenue and the receivables book that backs the securitized notes and supports the bank, so concentration, not leverage, is the first risk a committee should monitor.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings remain strong but are lower than a year earlier. Net earnings were USD 892 million in Q3 2026 against USD 1,077 million in the prior-year quarter, and USD 2,582 million for the nine months, while the net charge-off rate fell to 4.79% in Q3 2026 from 5.43% in Q2 2026. Retailer share arrangements of USD 3,193 million in the nine months move with program performance, so part of the benefit of better credit goes to partners and part of the pressure is absorbed by them. For debt service the only available proxy is 2.12x (pre-tax earnings plus interest expense, over interest expense, for the last twelve months), but that proxy includes deposit interest, is not an EBITDA measure, and the filings give no EBITDA.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Capital allocation is the main trend to monitor. Distributions in the nine months of 2026 were USD 3,262 million against net earnings of USD 2,582 million, which is 1.26x, while the common equity Tier 1 ratio on the recast basis moved from 13.5% at year-end 2025 to 12.9%, and borrowings to equity rose from 0.91x to 1.03x. New unsecured notes of USD 1,850 million and Series C preferred stock were issued in the same period. For creditors this means the equity buffer is being run down by choice and the company stays above stated regulatory minimums, so the pace of buybacks against capital targets is the variable to watch.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Structure matters for who holds which claim. Deposits are bank liabilities; securitized borrowings of USD 8,915 million are secured on restricted loans of USD 21,898 million, a ratio of 2.46x; the holding company owes about USD 7,511 million of senior and subordinated notes and relies on bank dividends and regulatory permission. Unsecured notes are 47.6% of borrowings, up from 44.6% at year-end 2025. The documented covenants restrict liens on and loss of control of the bank, and no leverage or restricted-payments test is visible, so legal capacity to distribute is not fully known.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Deposit funding is the largest strength: it is diversified between direct deposits of USD 76.2 billion and brokered deposits of USD 6.8 billion, and it lowers rollover risk relative to market funding. Liquidity is large and not dependent on committed bank lines: liquid assets were USD 19.5 billion and discount window capacity USD 13.0 billion. Credit quality was supportive in Q3 2026, with the net charge-off rate lower than in Q2 2026, delinquencies of 4.34% at 30 days and 2.06% at 90 days, and an allowance of 10.01% of receivables. Contract tenure is long, with expiry dates for the largest partners from 2030, and regulatory capital is stated as above minimums with the Bank well capitalized. Nothing documented shows sponsor extraction or creditor-adverse behaviour.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Concentration in five partner programs is the largest business weakness, and the partner purchase rights and termination terms are not in the sources. Earnings were below the prior-year quarter and a reserve build raised the provision. Distributions above earnings, a lower recast capital ratio and a rising unsecured share of borrowings reduce the margin beneath creditors. The structure places holding-company creditors behind deposits and trust investors for access to the bank's assets, and no parent-only statements for 2026 interim periods are available, so holding-company liquidity is stale at year-end 2025. Standard EBITDA leverage and cash interest cover cannot be computed.

spans.text: ## Request

Module: source readiness for Synchrony Financial (issuer id syf; NYSE ticker SYF; preferred depositary shares SYFPrA and SYFPrB), as of 2026-11-05, evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway credit_snapshot, public case, current period Q3 2026, prior period FY2025, reporting currency USD (all pinned sources report in US dollars; amounts are in millions unless a source says billions). Question: can the pinned source set support the requested minimum module set (CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5) and what remains blocked. This handoff gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it normalizes, reconciles and calculates no financial figure. The assertion for any later model objective is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED.

The run context (sha256 b7d2667de27eee9eaad22a8f2531b97f3d412b9a580fc12af95f3529015a7aad) holds user settings only. It names no deal terms, quotes, ratings, peers, legal documents, research questions or attachments, and it is not issuer evidence. Blank context values are not zero.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

| EX-99.1_2026-04-21_earningsrelease1q26.htm.jsonl | 0d50d951300ce2cbbde6c33a9c8f647888bd4c1a3c654b0abb8bb16574fa4c01 | 8 of 8 |
| EX-99.1_2026-07-21_earningsrelease2q26.htm.jsonl | 6450eda3e6d3c5e0b0af4323ee79065c818c4ce5b11bc0f800cb9d5d7e7bc639 | 7 of 7 |
| EX-99.1_2026-10-20_earningsrelease3q26.htm.jsonl | 79e5f3de157c7238c31f3c91c9d36532abc559b56d3ee90900d572761d0e13ee | 7 of 7 |

Also supplied and excluded as evidence: _retrieval.json, the pack's retrieval record (filing dates and accession numbers only, no issuer financial content; it carries no hash in this run and is not an issuer source). The first line of each extracted file states a sha256 of the original HTML; those differ from the extraction hashes above and the extraction hashes are the ones pinned by this run.
### Handoffs relied on
None. CP-0 is the first module and no handoff was supplied.
### Context
Run context file, sha256 b7d2667de27eee9eaad22a8f2531b97f3d412b9a580fc12af95f3529015a7aad (settings only, not evidence).
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings and releases are complete, current to the third quarter of 2026 and sufficient to start the snapshot work, with bounded limitations on non-GAAP detail, indenture terms and interim cash-paid items. | High | No financial supplement, presentation, indenture or securitization document is in the pack, so covenant terms and non-GAAP reconciliations rest on filing summaries only. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Filed statements and notes cover parent, bank and securitization-trust funding at the latest quarter end. | Debt, liquidity and capital work can be built from filed figures without management claims overriding them. | High |

| December 2025 capital ratios were recast in the latest quarterly filing, so the annual report and the latest quarter show different year-end ratios. | Any trend that mixes the two bases would misstate capital movement; the recast basis has to be used for comparisons. | High |
| Indenture covenants are described only generally, with no covenant terms or test levels. | Covenant headroom for the unsecured notes cannot be measured from this pack. | Medium |
| Cash paid for interest and taxes is printed for the full year only, not for interim periods. | Interim cash interest coverage cannot be built from filed cash-flow disclosure. | Medium |
### Readiness view

Readiness view: the pinned set supports the requested minimum module set with limitations. All four consumers are READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and none is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED, so the command sheet carries no DO NOT RUN entry. The strongest support is the latest quarterly report with its condensed statements, borrowing, capital and liquidity notes, backed by the annual report for full-year, parent-only and exhibit-index evidence and by two earlier quarterly reports for sequential periods. The strongest contrary evidence is that the filings summarise rather than reproduce the legal terms of the unsecured notes, that the earnings releases defer their detailed tables and non-GAAP reconciliation to a financial supplement that is not in the pack, and that year-end capital ratios were recast between the annual report and the latest quarterly report. Source sufficiency is not completion of downstream analysis; nothing here confirms that any later module will accept these inputs.
### Source assessment

Locators use the page number of the extracted source chunk (page:N), not the printed page. Coverage is of extracted text only; no chart, image or speaker-note content was inspected and text extraction is not a fidelity review.
| Source | Document family and authority | Entity and perimeter | Period and basis | Version relationship | Located evidence (exact quote) |

| 10-K FY2025 | Annual report on Form 10-K, filed statements; controls facts it states | Synchrony Financial consolidated, including Synchrony Bank and consolidated securitization entities; parent-only condensed statements are included | Fiscal year ended 2025-12-31, audited annual basis, USD millions | Original filing; the latest quarterly report recasts some December 2025 ratios | page:1 "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025" |

| 10-Q Q1 2026 | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q, unaudited filed statements | Synchrony Financial and subsidiaries, consolidated | Three months ended 2026-03-31 | Separate active source; not superseded by later quarters | page:1 "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026" |

| 10-Q Q2 2026 | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q, unaudited filed statements | Synchrony Financial and subsidiaries, consolidated | Three and six months ended 2026-06-30 | Separate active source; its capital table already shows December 2025 ratios recast for the software presentation change | page:1 "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026" |

| 10-Q Q3 2026 | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q, unaudited filed statements; latest filed period (signed 2026-10-22) | Synchrony Financial and subsidiaries, consolidated | Three and nine months ended 2026-09-30, with 2025-12-31 balance-sheet comparatives | Separate active source; supplies recast 2025-12-31 comparatives | page:1 "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026" |

| Earnings release Q1 2026 | Exhibit 99.1 earnings release; management narrative, attributed support | Synchrony Financial, consolidated | Three months ended 2026-03-31 | Narrative only; tables not included | page:1 "first quarter 2026 net earnings of $805 million" |

| Earnings release Q2 2026 | Exhibit 99.1 earnings release; management narrative, attributed support | Synchrony Financial, consolidated | Three months ended 2026-06-30 | Narrative only; tables not included | page:1 "second quarter 2026 net earnings of $885 million" |

| Earnings release Q3 2026 | Exhibit 99.1 earnings release; management narrative, attributed support, issued before the 10-Q | Synchrony Financial, consolidated | Three months ended 2026-09-30 | Narrative only; refers to a financial supplement not in the pack | page:1 "third quarter 2026 net earnings of $892 million" |
### Entity and instrument roles

The issuer is Synchrony Financial, the registrant and a savings and loan holding company. Its subsidiary Synchrony Bank is a separate obligor: the Bank issues its own senior unsecured notes and has its own capital tests. Consolidated securitization trusts (SYNCT, SFT, SYNIT) hold loan receivables and issue asset-backed notes owed to securitization investors. The filings state a single operating segment with five sales platforms, so no segment-level debt or restricted versus unrestricted entity split exists. There is no sponsor, guarantor or borrower distinct from the registrant in the context.

- Holding company status, page:29 of the annual report: "As a savings and loan holding company and financial holding company, Synchrony is subject to regulation, supervision and examination by the Federal Reserve Board."

- Parent-only statements exist, annual report page:193: "The following tables present parent company financial statements for Synchrony Financial"; page:194 notes "Includes investments in and amounts due from bank subsidiaries".
- Segment basis, latest quarterly report page:43: "Our single operating segment comprises a single reporting unit".

- Preferred stock, latest quarterly report page:1: "Series A SYFPrA"; Series C issuance, page:31: "in June 2026, we issued depositary shares representing $500 million of 7.250% fixed rate reset non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock, Series C".
### Conflicts, recasts and version distinctions
| Item | Source A and locator | Source B and locator | Downstream effect |

| Common equity Tier 1 at 2025-12-31 | Annual report page:188 "Common equity Tier 1 capital $ 13,242 12.6 %" | Latest quarterly report page:60 "Common equity Tier 1 Capital $ 14,290 13.5 % 4.5 %" | Disclosed recast, not an error. The latest quarterly report states at page:33 "Amounts and ratios at December 31, 2025 have been recast to reflect the change in presentation of internal-use capitalized software". CP-1 must label the basis and not mix the two year-end figures. The annual report is not edited by the recast and stays the authority for the originally reported ratio. |

| Prior-year ratios in the Q3 release | Release page:4 "Prior period amounts have been recast to reflect the change in presentation of internal-use capitalized software" | Annual report page:188 (original basis) | The release states recast comparatives that the pack cannot tie to a recast table, because the financial supplement is absent. |

| Net earnings, three quarterly sources | Releases page:1 of each (quoted above) | Matching condensed statements of earnings in each quarterly report | No conflict found in net earnings between release and filing for any of the three quarters; the filed statement controls if later differences arise. |

Duplicates: the annual report and the quarterly reports overlap on balance-sheet comparatives (2025-12-31); the annual report is retained for the originally reported value and the latest quarterly report for the recast value. No hash duplicates exist among the seven sources.
### Coverage by source profile

- Financial reports: statements of earnings, comprehensive income, financial position, equity and cash flows, and notes, are all present in the latest quarterly report and the annual report (index at latest quarterly report page:2 and annual report page:202). Borrowings note, latest quarterly report page:57 "Total borrowings $ 17,025 $ 15,182"; balance sheet, page:39 "Total borrowings 17,025 15,182"; unsecured note ladder, page:28 "Total senior and subordinated unsecured notes $ 8,150"; securitized maturities, page:26 "Total borrowings—owed to securitization investors $ 3,900 $ 5,025 $ — $ — $ 8,925". Facility-level debt is therefore located. Carrying value and principal are shown on different bases (unamortised discounts, premiums and issuance costs), which CP-1 must keep apart.

- Liquidity and funding: latest quarterly report page:29 "$19.5 billion of liquid assets" and "we had an aggregate of $13.0 billion of available borrowing capacity through the Federal Reserve’s discount window"; annual report page:91 "we had an aggregate of $2.1 billion of undrawn credit facilities". Cash flows: page:41 "Total cash and equivalents, including restricted amounts, at end of period $ 16,697 $ 16,287".
- Capital: latest quarterly report page:60 "Synchrony Financial met all minimum capital requirements" and the capital table quoted above.

- Covenants: latest quarterly report page:28 "We were in compliance with all of these covenants at September 30, 2026"; annual report page:57 "we were not in default under any of our credit facilities". Only a general statement is supplied.
- Securitization triggers: latest quarterly report page:27 "No early amortization event has occurred". Subsequent event within the filing: page:27 "which matured and were repaid in October 2026".

- Business and transaction narrative: annual report page:9 "Home & Auto accounted for $5.7 billion, or 26%, of our total interest and fees on loans for the year ended December 31, 2025"; acquisition, latest quarterly report page:47 "In April 2026, we completed our acquisition of the Lowe's commercial co-branded credit card portfolio". No sponsor-led or merger transaction is in the sources.

- Earnings releases: reported and management-framed figures with year-on-year comparisons for a quarter only; no quarter versus year-to-date table, no guidance table and no reconciliation. Release page:7 "please see the detailed financial tables and information that follow", and page:4 "See the financial supplement for additional information", but the supplement is not in the pack.

- Legal and financing sources: none supplied as executed documents. Annual report page:202 lists "Indenture, dated as of August 11, 2014, between Synchrony Financial and The Bank of New York Mellon, as Trustee" by reference only. Legal proceedings: latest quarterly report page:65 "NOTE 15. LEGAL PROCEEDINGS AND REGULATORY MATTERS" (general disclosure).

- Interim cash paid: annual report page:151 "Cash paid during the year for interest $ (4,162)" and page:193 "Total income taxes paid $ 710" are full-year only; the quarterly cash-flow statement in the latest quarterly report (page:41) shows no supplemental cash-paid lines.

- Ratings: latest quarterly report page:28 "Senior unsecured debt BBB- BBB" is the issuer's own table of agency ratings; no agency report is in the pack, so ratings are an attributed issuer statement.
### Consumer readiness
| Consumer | Status | Evidence demand and basis | Carried limitations |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Financial statements, debt ladders, liquidity, capital, discrete and year-to-date periods are located in filings; facility-level debt and carrying values are present. | No financial supplement or non-GAAP reconciliation; no interim cash-paid interest and tax; no indenture terms; recast December 2025 capital basis. |

| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business model, five sales platforms, partner relationships, regulation, the Lowe's commercial portfolio acquisition and 2026 capital actions are located in the annual and quarterly reports. | No presentation or call transcript; partner agreements and contract terms not supplied; no ownership or sponsor structure applies (listed equity). |
| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Consumes only CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, so no source gap is added; the dependency planner sequences it. | Inherits the CP-1 and CP-1A limitations above. |

| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Validates quotes and figures against the prepared pack; the filings supply locatable quotes for every material area. | Extracted text only, so chart or image content cannot be checked; inherits upstream limitations. |
Command sheet: no consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED, so no DO NOT RUN entry arises.
### Evidence to risk to consequence

- Evidence: the latest quarterly report gives funding by instrument family (securitized, unsecured, deposits) and a covenant compliance statement, but the indentures are only incorporated by reference. Source risk: the unsecured notes' covenant package, events of default and any cross-default or acceleration terms cannot be read, only the issuer's compliance statement. Consequence: covenant headroom and legal ranking are recorded as Not supplied, and CP-1 must not present covenant tests as measured.

- Evidence: year-end capital ratios differ between the annual report and the latest quarterly report because of a disclosed presentation change. Source risk: a trend line that joins the two bases would show a spurious capital change. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must state the basis of each ratio and use the recast basis for sequential comparison.

- Evidence: the releases name a financial supplement and a non-GAAP reconciliation that are absent. Source risk: tangible common equity, return on tangible common equity and the recast comparatives rest on management statements. Consequence: these metrics stay attributed management claims, and a filing figure controls whenever the two differ.

- Evidence: full-year cash paid for interest and taxes appears only in the annual report. Source risk: interim coverage measures lack a cash-paid input. Consequence: such measures are Not calculable for Q3 2026 and the nine-month period from filed cash-paid data.

- Evidence: the entity roles span holding company, bank and consolidated trusts. Source risk: trust assets support trust notes and bank deposits fund the bank, so consolidated totals can hide structural subordination. Consequence: downstream debt work should split parent, bank and securitization claims and not rely on a single consolidated total.
### Subsequent events and cutoff

The latest filing was signed 2026-10-22, before the cutoff of 2026-11-05, and the latest release is dated 2026-10-20. The latest quarterly report records an October 2026 securitized repayment (quoted above) and states at page:60 "There are no conditions or events subsequent to September 30, 2026" that changed capital category. No source in the pack is dated after the cutoff. Events between 2026-10-22 and 2026-11-05 are not covered by any pinned source.

No financial figure was calculated, normalized or reconciled in this module, in line with the method. Coverage counts only:

## Gaps

| Financial supplement and non-GAAP reconciliation referenced by the Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 releases are not supplied; the releases carry narrative only (Not supplied) | Medium | CP-1, CP-5 | Add the supplements or treat tangible metrics as attributed management claims |

| Indentures and supplemental indentures (incorporated by reference in the annual report exhibit index and the Q3 2026 report) and securitization documents are not supplied; covenant terms and tests are Not calculable | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Add the executed notes documents if covenant analysis is required |
| Cash paid for interest and taxes is printed for FY2025 only; interim amounts are Not supplied | Low | CP-1 | Use full-year figures only, or add interim disclosure if it exists elsewhere |

| Recast December 2025 capital ratios differ from the annual report; the recast reconciliation table is not in the pack | Medium | CP-1, CP-2, CP-5 | Label basis on every capital figure; add the supplement for the recast bridge |
| Earnings presentations, call transcripts and partner agreements are not supplied | Low | CP-1A, CP-2 | Business narrative relies on the annual report and quarterly reports only |
| Agency rating reports are not supplied; ratings come from the issuer's own table | Low | CP-1, CP-2 | Treat ratings as attributed issuer statements |
| Charts, images and tables rendered as graphics in the filings are not inspected; extraction is text only | Low | CP-5 | Do not claim chart-based figures |
| The pack has no source dated 2026-10-23 to 2026-11-05 | Low | All | Subsequent events in that window are Not supplied |
## Next module

CP-1 (financial and capital structure data), using the Q3 2026 quarterly report as the primary period source, the FY2025 annual report for the full-year and prior-period basis, and the two earlier 2026 quarterly reports for sequential quarters. It must carry forward the recast capital basis, the carrying value versus principal distinction in debt, and the absent covenant terms and non-GAAP reconciliation. CP-1A can proceed in parallel on the business and transaction narrative.

### Financial base view

Financial base view: the pinned filings give a complete reported base for the consolidated issuer at four balance-sheet dates (FY2025, Q1 2026, Q2 2026, Q3 2026) and for the nine months of 2026, with year-on-year comparatives. Leverage in the sense the chart tables ask for is Not supplied because the issuer reports no EBITDA and treats interest expense as an operating cost within net interest income. The funding structure is deposit-led, with securitized borrowings and unsecured notes as the borrowed layers; the unsecured layer grew most in 2026 through the February and July issuances. Capital is reported above the stated minimums and the Company and the Bank are stated as well capitalized, but year-end 2025 capital ratios exist on two bases because of a presentation recast, and one earlier handoff statement is corrected below. Interim cash-paid interest and tax are Not supplied, so no cash interest cover can be built for 2026 periods. Nothing in this base is a credit opinion; the CP-2 synthesis owns that.

Seniority and guarantees: the filings print the instruments by issuer and describe no guarantee between Synchrony Financial and the Bank notes. Deposits, securitization investors and unsecured noteholders are different claimants on different asset pools, and the trust notes are secured on restricted loans while the unsecured notes are not. Ranking among them is not printed as a legal waterfall and is outside this base.
### Claims outside the borrowings line

- Deposits (82,951 at Q3 2026) are the main funding source; the issuer states direct deposits of 76.2 billion and brokered deposits of 6.8 billion, and an estimated uninsured portion of 7.1 billion (10-Q Q3 pages:25 and 26). They are inside total liabilities and outside the borrowings line.
- Unused customer credit card lines of approximately 455 billion at 2026-09-30 are unconditionally cancellable and are not funded obligations (10-Q Q3 page:53).
- Investment commitments of 200 for affordable housing and related variable interest entities are due between 2026 and 2046 (10-Q Q3 page:56).
- Retailer share arrangements are a contra-revenue sharing cost, 3,193 in the nine months of 2026, not a debt claim.

- Legal and regulatory matters: Note 15 states that estimated reasonably possible losses are immaterial and prints no amount, and that no pending matter is believed to have a material adverse effect on financial condition or liquidity (10-Q Q3 page:65).

- Lease obligations, pensions and purchase commitments: the 10-K says the Stamford headquarters site is leased (page:199) but no lease liability line or amount was located in a search of the sources; Not supplied.
### Liquidity, capital and ratings

- Liquid assets of 19.5 billion at 2026-09-30 (16.6 billion at 2025-12-31); discount window availability of 13.0 billion; undrawn securitization capacity of 2.6 billion of which 2.1 billion is committed and 450 million uncommitted (10-Q Q3 page:29). Loans pledged by the Bank to the discount window were 18.4 billion (10-Q Q3 page:47).

- Capital: the Company and the Bank are stated as meeting well-capitalized requirements (10-Q Q3 page:60). On the recast basis the common equity Tier 1 ratio moved from 13.5 percent at 2025-12-31 to 13.2 percent at Q2 2026 and 12.9 percent at Q3 2026, alongside purchases of treasury stock of 2,878 and common dividends of 314 in the nine months of 2026 (10-Q Q3 pages:60 and 41). The parent relies on Bank dividends; 10-K Note 16 shows parent-only cash and equivalents of 2,465 at 2025-12-31 and dividends from bank subsidiaries of 2,700 in FY2025, with restricted net assets of subsidiaries of 14.7 billion (10-K pages:193 and 194). No parent-only statements are printed for 2026 interim periods.

- Ratings as printed by the issuer: Synchrony Financial senior unsecured BBB- (S&P) and BBB (Fitch); outlook Positive at S&P and Stable at Fitch at 2026-09-30, against Stable at both at 2025-12-31 (10-Q Q3 page:28; 10-K page:57). The agency reports are not in the pack.

- Covenants: the 10-K describes the indenture covenants as restrictions on disposing of or placing liens on the Bank voting stock and on any merger or sale that leaves the Bank less than 80 percent controlled; compliance and no default are stated (10-K page:57; 10-Q Q3 page:28). No leverage or coverage maintenance test is printed.
### Corrections to the earlier handoff and definition risks

- Correction to the source readiness handoff: that handoff recorded covenant terms as supplied only in general terms; the annual report does state the covenant types (control of the Bank at 80 percent and lien and disposal limits on its voting stock), as quoted above. Test levels and the full indenture text remain unavailable. The earlier handoff is not edited and this answer governs.

- Capital recast: year-end 2025 common equity Tier 1 appears as 12.6 percent in the annual report and 13.5 percent in the Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 reports, because internal-use capitalized software was reclassified from intangible assets (10-K page:149 intangible assets 1,255; 10-Q Q3 page:39 intangible assets 104 for the same date). The Q1 2026 ratio is on the earlier basis, so the move from Q1 to Q2 2026 mixes a basis change with performance.
- Carrying value and principal differ by unamortised discounts, premiums and issuance costs; the chart tables use principal, the financials table uses carrying value.

- Asset acquisition: the annual report expected the Lowe's commercial portfolio at about 0.8 billion; the completed purchase in April 2026 was 0.7 billion (10-K page:34; 10-Q Q3 page:47). The filed completed figure controls.

- Net earnings fell against the prior-year third quarter (892 against 1,077); the Q3 2026 release attributes this to a higher provision for credit losses (a reserve build against a reserve release in the prior-year quarter), higher other expense and higher retailer share arrangements, partly offset by higher net interest income (release page:2, attributed management statement). Nine-month net charge-offs fell (3,946 against 4,297, 10-Q Q3 page:14).
### Subsequent events and cutoff

The latest filing is the Q3 2026 report signed 2026-10-22. It records that 750 of fixed securitized borrowings were repaid in October 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:57) and states no events after 2026-09-30 that changed the capital category (page:60). Q3 2026 results were released on 2026-10-20 before the 10-Q. No source covers 2026-10-23 to 2026-11-05.

All inputs are reported figures in US dollars millions from the cited pages; results are rounded to the stated precision.

### Borrowings against principal and carrying value (Q3 2026)
- Principal: securitized 8,925 plus unsecured 8,150 equals 17,075.
- Carrying: securitized 8,915 plus unsecured 8,110 equals 17,025, matching total borrowings on the balance sheet.
- Difference between principal and carrying: 10 for securitized, 40 for unsecured, 50 in total (17,075 less 17,025).

- Unsecured principal ladder: Synchrony Financial fixed 1,000 + 650 + 750 = 2,400; fixed-to-floating 750 + 800 + 500 + 500 + 750 + 600 + 500 = 4,400; Bank 600; subordinated 750; total 2,400 + 4,400 + 600 + 750 = 8,150, matching the printed total.
- Maturity table total: 3,900 + 5,025 + 8,150 = 17,075.

- Unsecured notes as a share of total borrowings (carrying): FY2025 6,767 / 15,182 = 44.6 percent; Q3 2026 8,110 / 17,025 = 47.6 percent. Securitized borrowings rose from 8,415 to 8,915 and unsecured notes from 6,767 to 8,110, so of the increase of 1,843 in total borrowings, 1,343 is unsecured and 500 is securitized.

The proxy uses accrued, not cash, interest expense and includes deposit interest, which is an operating cost of the bank; it is not EBITDA over cash interest and must not be compared to leveraged-finance covenants.
### Liquidity
| Period | Cash and equivalents | Undrawn committed securitization capacity | Sum |

The sum is not a liquidity total: undrawn capacity is subject to borrowing conditions and cash includes cash in transit that the issuer excludes from its liquidity portfolio. Letters of credit are not applicable; none was found in a search of the sources.
### Securitization collateral

Restricted loans of consolidated securitization entities over securitized borrowings: 21,898 / 8,915 = 2.46x at Q3 2026 and 22,400 / 8,415 = 2.66x at FY2025 (10-Q Q3 page:39). This is a balance-sheet ratio, not a trust-level credit enhancement measure.
### Maturities by horizon from 2026-09-30

Due within one year to 2027-09-30: securitized 3,900 (of which 750 was repaid in October 2026) plus the Bank notes due August 2027 of 600 equals 4,500, against liquid assets of 19.5 billion (19,500) at 2026-09-30. Unsecured principal due by end of 2027: 600 + 1,000 = 1,600. The Synchrony Financial notes due December 2027 (1,000) fall after the one-year point.

### Credit translations

- Revenue durability: Evidence: the five largest programs were 54 percent of interest and fees, with expiry dates from 2030 to 2035 (F1, 10-K pages:13, 14). Risk mechanic: a single non-renewal or a partner purchase of accounts would remove a large block of receivables and fee income, while long terms give visibility to the contract dates. Credit implication: monitoring posture should track renewals and partner health; revenue visibility is high until 2030 and concentrated afterwards. The counter-evidence is the extension of the Amazon agreement and the new OnePay programme in 2025.

- Margin and cash-flow risk: Evidence: retailer share payments rose while net charge-offs fell (F14), and other expense rose with technology and operating losses. Risk mechanic: the sharing of program performance caps the benefit of better credit, so margin gains from lower losses are shared, while cost growth is not shared. Credit implication: debt service capacity is supported by earnings that remain well above interest cost, but margin resilience depends on credit staying at current levels. The earnings fall against the prior-year quarter is a named counter to a stable-margin view.

- Concentration risk: Evidence: three partners each over a tenth of interest and fees (F1). Risk mechanic: partner financial distress or a pricing dispute would affect volume, receivables quality and share payments together. Credit implication: concentration should be a monitoring item; no recovery conclusion is drawn here.

- Capital allocation and sponsor alignment: Evidence: distributions exceeded net earnings in the nine months alongside new securities issuance (Ownership, governance and capital allocation). Risk mechanic: returning capital faster than it is earned lowers the equity cushion, and new senior notes at the holding company add claims that rank behind the Bank's deposits and the trusts' secured notes in terms of asset access. Credit implication: the key uncertainty is the pace of buybacks against the capital ratio and rating-agency targets; no sponsor exists to provide external support.

- Key uncertainties: executed indentures, contract terms, ownership percentages and the financial supplement are Not supplied; a logged conflict of presentation (the capital recast) counters any simple year-over-year capital trend.

### Credit view

Synchrony Financial has a sound fundamental credit profile with moderate, identifiable risks. The strongest support is deposit-led funding (USD 82,951 million of deposits against USD 17,025 million of borrowings at 2026-09-30), liquid assets of USD 19.5 billion and a common equity Tier 1 ratio of 12.9% that the company states exceeds regulatory minimums, with a net charge-off rate of 4.79% in Q3 2026. The weakest point is concentration: five partner programs produced 54% of interest and fees, and distributions of USD 3,262 million in the nine months of 2026 exceeded net earnings of USD 2,582 million. What decides the outcome is whether partners renew and credit losses stay near current levels while buybacks continue to lower the capital ratio.
### Key findings

Synchrony Financial funds its balance sheet mainly with deposits, which were USD 82,951 million at 2026-09-30 and 83% of funding sources, while borrowings were USD 17,025 million. Because debt due within one year of that date was USD 4,500 million against liquid assets of USD 19.5 billion, near-term maturities are covered several times by liquidity even before counting the USD 2,100 million of undrawn committed securitization capacity. This lowers refinancing and liquidity risk for creditors, and the main condition is continued access to deposits and the Federal Reserve discount window, whose availability was USD 13.0 billion.

The business depends on a short list of partners. The five largest programs produced 54% of interest and fees and 52% of loan receivables at year-end 2025, and three of them each exceeded a tenth of interest and fees; contract expiry dates run from 2030 to 2035, and some agreements let the partner buy the accounts on termination. A loss or repricing of one program would reduce revenue and the receivables book that backs the securitized notes and supports the bank, so concentration, not leverage, is the first risk a committee should monitor.

Earnings remain strong but are lower than a year earlier. Net earnings were USD 892 million in Q3 2026 against USD 1,077 million in the prior-year quarter, and USD 2,582 million for the nine months, while the net charge-off rate fell to 4.79% in Q3 2026 from 5.43% in Q2 2026. Retailer share arrangements of USD 3,193 million in the nine months move with program performance, so part of the benefit of better credit goes to partners and part of the pressure is absorbed by them. For debt service the only available proxy is 2.12x (pre-tax earnings plus interest expense, over interest expense, for the last twelve months), but that proxy includes deposit interest, is not an EBITDA measure, and the filings give no EBITDA.

Capital allocation is the main trend to monitor. Distributions in the nine months of 2026 were USD 3,262 million against net earnings of USD 2,582 million, which is 1.26x, while the common equity Tier 1 ratio on the recast basis moved from 13.5% at year-end 2025 to 12.9%, and borrowings to equity rose from 0.91x to 1.03x. New unsecured notes of USD 1,850 million and Series C preferred stock were issued in the same period. For creditors this means the equity buffer is being run down by choice and the company stays above stated regulatory minimums, so the pace of buybacks against capital targets is the variable to watch.

Structure matters for who holds which claim. Deposits are bank liabilities; securitized borrowings of USD 8,915 million are secured on restricted loans of USD 21,898 million, a ratio of 2.46x; the holding company owes about USD 7,511 million of senior and subordinated notes and relies on bank dividends and regulatory permission. Unsecured notes are 47.6% of borrowings, up from 44.6% at year-end 2025. The documented covenants restrict liens on and loss of control of the bank, and no leverage or restricted-payments test is visible, so legal capacity to distribute is not fully known.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Deposit funding is the largest strength: it is diversified between direct deposits of USD 76.2 billion and brokered deposits of USD 6.8 billion, and it lowers rollover risk relative to market funding. Liquidity is large and not dependent on committed bank lines: liquid assets were USD 19.5 billion and discount window capacity USD 13.0 billion. Credit quality was supportive in Q3 2026, with the net charge-off rate lower than in Q2 2026, delinquencies of 4.34% at 30 days and 2.06% at 90 days, and an allowance of 10.01% of receivables. Contract tenure is long, with expiry dates for the largest partners from 2030, and regulatory capital is stated as above minimums with the Bank well capitalized. Nothing documented shows sponsor extraction or creditor-adverse behaviour.

Weaknesses. Concentration in five partner programs is the largest business weakness, and the partner purchase rights and termination terms are not in the sources. Earnings were below the prior-year quarter and a reserve build raised the provision. Distributions above earnings, a lower recast capital ratio and a rising unsecured share of borrowings reduce the margin beneath creditors. The structure places holding-company creditors behind deposits and trust investors for access to the bank's assets, and no parent-only statements for 2026 interim periods are available, so holding-company liquidity is stale at year-end 2025. Standard EBITDA leverage and cash interest cover cannot be computed.
